extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting to or reviewing for eLife (authors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and policies governing how eLife selects, reviews, and publishes manuscripts, including desired paper qualities, article-type requirements, editorial decision-making, revision expectations, and transparency of post-review records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities of published papers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our goal at eLife is to publish papers that our reviewers and editors find authoritative, rigorous, insightful, enlightening or just beautiful"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the high-level evaluative attributes editors and reviewers use to judge submissions; authors should aim to produce work that meets one or more of these descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article type definitions and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife publishes Research Articles (with no limits to the length or number of figures), Short Reports, Tools and Resources, and Research Advances (substantial developments that build on previous eLife papers). eLife also publishes Magazine content such as Editorials, Feature Articles, and Insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult the Author Guide and Policies for details and requirements for each submission type; article type determines scope and expectations (e.g., Research Articles have no length/figure limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by working scientist editors (editorial judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We rely on the judgment of the working scientists who serve as our editors to select papers for peer review and publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no artificial acceptance-rate target; editorial selection is based on the scientific judgment of practicing researchers rather than quota or metric-driven rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance on Impact Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and publication decisions are not justified or driven by journal-level Impact Factor metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and collaborative peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our goal is to make peer review constructive and collaborative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and editorial interactions are expected to focus on constructive criticism and collaboration between reviewers, editors, and authors to improve the work rather than adversarial gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is a process standard: authors can expect prompt initial editorial decisions on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working scientists make all editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors who are active researchers (rather than professional editors without research responsibilities) lead decisions about peer review and publication, implying decisions are grounded in current disciplinary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated, concise revision requests
rubrics_metrics.description: "Revision requests are consolidated following an open, internal consultation among reviewers to deliver a single, concise set of the essential revisions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than multiple, potentially conflicting reviewer lists, eLife consolidates reviewer input into one prioritized set of essential revisions for authors to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of post-review records
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review decisions and author responses for published papers are available for all to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife publishes the decision letters and author responses alongside published articles to promote transparency about the review process and revisions made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Author Guide for metrics and detailed editorial process information
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in our Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For operational details, timelines, and numerical metrics, authors and reviewers should consult the Author Guide and Policies linked from the page.
